Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testConcurrentModification` is performing an element-wise multiplication (ebeMultiply) of two OpenMapRealVector instances. The bug report indicates a MathRuntimeException when using ebeMultiply on OpenMapRealVector.

Analyzing the `ebeMultiply` method in `OpenMapRealVector`, it:
- Verifies the dimension of the input vector `v`.
- Creates a new OpenMapRealVector `res` copied from `this`.
- Iterates over the internal map `entries` of `res`, performing element-wise multiplication of each entry by the corresponding element in vector `v`.
The iteration uses `res.entries.iterator()`. 

The internal `entries` field is of type `OpenIntToDoubleHashMap` which has an `Iterator` class, that saves a modification count `referenceCount` on construction, presumably to detect concurrent modifications. The constructor calls `advance()` during initialization.

The concurrency issue likely arises because `res.setEntry()` modifies the `entries` underlying the iterator `iter` itself (since `res` uses the same internal map), causing the `OpenIntToDoubleHashMap.Iterator` to detect that the map was concurrently modified during iteration, resulting in the exception.

Hence the root cause is that the `ebeMultiply` method modifies the underlying map (`res.entries`) in the middle of iterating over this same map, which is not allowed. The modification count mechanism inside `OpenIntToDoubleHashMap.Iterator` detects this and throws the runtime exception.

This explains why a seemingly simple element-wise multiplication leads to a MathRuntimeException due to concurrent modification of the underlying hash map in `OpenMapRealVector`.

This diagnosis matches the test code and the bug report symptoms perfectly.

Next, I will suggest which methods to fix.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
